We need to assume a typical development team (but we are the sole developer). Effort includes design, implementation, unit testing, integration testing, documentation, etc. We'll break down into activities per user story or per component.

AWS source/sink: using existing Spring Integration AWS extension, so integration effort, but still need to implement adapters. Cassandra sink: implementing a new sink module for Cassandra. - All modules will follow existing Spring Integration configuration style (XML, Java config, annotations).
- Assuming existing project structure with Maven/Gradle, continuous integration.

- The data partition strategy feature is already implemented in GA, so only testing is needed.
- No need for UI or user-facing changes; purely backend modules.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Integration's channel adapter pattern for all source and sink modules to ensure consistency with the existing framework.
Leverage existing Spring Integration AWS extension as a reference, but implement custom adapters for S3 and SES to align with the specific user stories.
For WebSocket source, utilize Spring WebSocket support and Spring Integration's WebSocket integration (from the referenced repository) to create a channel adapter.
For Cassandra sink, use Spring Data Cassandra or the Cassandra Java driver and implement an outbound channel adapter.
For HAWQ sink, implement using PXF (Pivotal Extension Framework) and convert data to Avro/Parquet format using Apache Avro and Parquet libraries.
For SOLR sink, use SolrJ client and implement an indexing outbound channel adapter.
Error channel configuration will follow Spring Integration's error handling patterns, allowing definition of exception hierarchies and custom catch exceptions via configuration.
All modules will support both XML and Java configuration styles as per Spring Integration conventions.
Assume existing project structure with Maven/Gradle build, continuous integration, and dependency management already in place.
assumptions: Developer has deep knowledge of Spring Framework, Spring Integration, Java 17+, and the relevant third-party libraries.
The existing codebase already includes build system, dependency management, and CI/CD pipeline; no setup effort is required.
Third-party libraries (e.g., Cassandra driver, SolrJ, Avro, Parquet, AWS SDK) are available and compatible with the project.
External systems (Cassandra, SOLR, HAWQ, AWS) can be mocked for unit tests or made available via Docker for integration tests.
The data partition strategy feature (U8) is already implemented in the GA release; only testing effort is needed.
No user interface changes are required; all development is backend module implementation.
Documentation includes API docs and usage examples for each module.
Effort estimates assume a single developer working full-time (8-hour days) without interruptions.

activities.activity_description: Review user stories, design high-level architecture, define module interfaces, common patterns, and configuration approach for all new source/sink modules and error channel.
Implement WebSocket source channel adapter using Spring WebSocket and Spring Integration WebSocket support. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and basic integration test.
Implement AWS source (S3, SES) and AWS sink (S3) channel adapters leveraging the existing Spring Integration AWS extension as reference. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and integration tests.
Implement Cassandra sink outbound channel adapter using Spring Data Cassandra or direct driver. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and basic integration test.
Implement HAWQ sink channel adapter via PXF extension with Avro/Parquet format conversion. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and integration test.
Implement SOLR sink outbound channel adapter using SolrJ for full-text indexing. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and integration test.

Implement configurable error channel mechanism supporting exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException) and custom catch patterns. Includes design, coding, unit tests, and integration test.
Test the existing data partition strategy state preservation feature to ensure it works when modules are added/deleted. Includes test case design, execution, and bug fixes if needed.
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all new modules together, system-level testing, and regression testing. Includes test environment setup and test execution.
Write API documentation, usage examples, and configuration guides for all new modules. Prepare release notes and package the increment for delivery.
